messages.subject: Selection of feeding areas
parts:
Hi all,

I've been working on some crowned eagle data (territorial adults) with the GPS data behaviourally annotated as 'feeding and not feeding'. I'm interested in understanding what parts of the landscape crowned eagles are using to feed (i.e., process their prey and feed) relative to the habitat composition of their territory. 

I've been considering using an RSF for this, and after reading through some of the group threads, just wanted some confirmation that this is okay to do.

1. calculate aKDE per individual (data spanning over 1-3 years approx per bird) with all feeding+non-feeding data

2. in rsf.fit, use only the feeding points (e.g., one point from one cluster per day with minimum 3 hours or longer in between, I have seen that these need to be independent) and compare this to the individuals' territory aKDE. So basically,
  • rsf.fit(bird_independent_feeding, bird_territory_akde, R = env_layers, integrator = "Reimann") 
Is this allowed/ appropriate to do? Or must feeding locations be compared specifically to the aKDEs from feeding locations only (and not all the feeding+non-feeding data defining the territory)? 

3. Can I then estimate the mean for the population?  

Apologies for some redundancy here, whether step 2 in particular is suitable was not clear to me from the previous conversations on the group.

Thank you so very much! 
Varalika
